title: KFTD: Koopman-Fourier Time-Differentiable Network for Continuous Ocean Spatiotemporal Forecasting

problem.claim: Ocean spatiotemporal forecasting must model complex dynamical systems while remaining computationally efficient.

gap.claim: Pure data-driven approaches face a physical-consistency bottleneck, while diffusion models require multi-step noise sampling.

contributions.claim: A time-continuous two-stage KFTD Network decouples interpolation from prediction for efficient and scalable spatiotemporal modeling.
The method maps nonlinear dynamics into Koopman linear space, uses Fourier analysis for arbitrary-sub-step interpolation, and applies a lightweight residual network for final forecasting.
D-PP Loss supports arbitrary PDE constraints end to end.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a 4× computational speed-up relative to diffusion-model processing.
Across four ocean datasets, the authors report an average MSE reduction of 5.6%, reaching 12.7% for SST.
The authors report a 76.25% efficiency improvement over MCVD.

narrative_sequence.summary: Ocean forecasting supports climate monitoring and disaster early-warning.
Forecasting must address complex dynamics and computational efficiency simultaneously.
KFTD separates continuous-time interpolation from prediction using Koopman–Fourier modeling and a residual predictor.
The framework avoids multi-step noise sampling and supports PDE constraints through D-PP Loss.
Experiments on four ocean datasets report lower MSE and improved efficiency.

source_observation.claim: Separating interpolation from prediction enables arbitrary-sub-step continuous-time modeling.

interpretation.claim: A staged architecture can allocate specialized components to state reconstruction and forecast generation.

application.claim: Use continuous-time interpolation plus a lightweight predictor when forecasts require flexible temporal resolution and efficiency.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition generalizes beyond the reported ocean datasets.

source_observation.claim: D-PP Loss incorporates arbitrary PDE constraints end to end.

interpretation.claim: Embedding physical constraints in training may address consistency limitations in purely data-driven forecasting.

application.claim: Consider differentiable PDE-aware objectives for scientific forecasting systems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the PDEs, constraint formulations, or their effect on individual datasets.

unknowns: The four datasets and their exact task configurations are unspecified.
Evaluation protocols, baseline details, and statistical variation are unspecified.
The PDE constraints and D-PP Loss formulation are unspecified.
The source does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
